claims.claim: Reviewers describe the in-game tutorial as broken or non-functional, failing to register completed tasks or soft-locking during progression.

citations.review_text:
The tutorial does not function at a technical level.
- The 'run through the basic controls' tasks don't reliably register that you've done them. A switch-to-third-person-mode task doesn't register while you're still in the vehicle that you started in, without the tutorial giving you any indication that you're supposed to leave the vehicle at that point.
- Tells you to toggle something while flying. I took a couple seconds longer at a previous task, so I'm out of fuel and can't fly anymore. No instructions on how to refuel included. Guess I'll restart and try to speed run the previous steps so I can actually do the tutorial.
- "go mine some stuff and pick the rocks". I pick up the rocks, tutorial does not register that I've done that. No idea what wonky side-condition I'm missing this time, but at this point I've run out of patience. A game is supposed to be about having fun, not about getting frustrated at bugs. Refund it is.

Never have I ever given a bad review to a game.

Well, today's the day.

The tutorial kept on soft-locking me, or whatever it is, "Quick-start". Couldn't understand how to destroy stuff for the first 10 minutes. The trailer was SO different from this "garbage".

I was expecting something like trailmakers + no man's sky + stellaris. This was so much worse.

I couldn't figure out how to move building blocks, because the tutorial was terrible. I couldn't... for the life of me, figure out how I was so excited about this before I bought it.

Building makes me want to refund the game, which I most probably will! 90% of the game is behind two thousand DLCs. I bought three, and I only unlocked like, 13 building blocks or, whatever the hell.

3/10, I do NOT recommend this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks clear instructions or an effective in-game tutorial for learning core mechanics.

citations.review_text:
No clear tutorial, game hints just say "figure it out", nonsensical crafting path (took me 2 hours to realize that stones make iron ingots(???)), and etc.
I thought it would be a cool space game, but it's so unintuitive, that I just walked around without knowing what to do for 2 hours straight.

This game does not do a good job of explaining why it's enjoyable, or even how to even get comfortable with the controls and main gameplay loop. The tutorial is hidden inside a submenu, and weirdly enough there's even a popup suggesting that you do not go inside the submenu where the tutorial is. The tutorial consists of a series of nonspecific text boxes, which is not nearly enough compared to the amount of menus this game throws at you.

Absolutely ridiculous.  10 years later and still no scroll to change weapon, tab to open inventory, no tutorial, quick start is basically minecraft without any of the fun.  I was an early supporter, but apparently i velieved in the game more than the developers did.

Directionless. Unguided. Left to drift. Tutorial "bot" wastes 2 hours making player do WASD and jetpack circus tricks, sends you off to drill for rocks, then leaves you figure out how to build the first block it wants.

No words about possible threats you should be concerned about.

Then wolves kill you in the night. You respawn in the same place and they kill you. Respawn again and they kill you again.

The YouTube videos in the Help are over 7 years old with visuals, screens, and menus also from 7 years ago.

Wanted to play space engineers from all the cool videos and recommendations over the years, instead played "manual mining drill and Computer crash simulator".  In addition, the tutorial says to do something but doesn't tell you how.

citations.review_text: When I was little I used to play this game with legos, I tried the game for the first time now and I can assure you the lego version is 1000 times easier. Watch a tutorial first before starting your game and expect a long grind to build things, so far it is fun tho

The game is a sack of shit. The tutorials are hard to follow (with a message on screen that disappears before you even know what's going on).
Surviving when you first start is a ridiculously difficult grind. You have to mine a stupendous amount of stone to obtain a small amount of ingots to craft plates. I'd say you have to mine stone for like 30-45 minutes just to build one platform which costs 400 plates. Fuck that.

Let's get on to the other thing, you start with a shitty rover which has a survival kit built in. The survival kit is used to craft everything. If you so much as knock your rover against anything, the kit is damaged and there's no way to repair it without Construction Comps, and guess what these are crafted in the kit.
It's so easy to flip this shitty vehicle over on the fucking shitty terrain! And when its dark you can't see anything when driving around, the headlights project light just 3 metres ahead. THERE IS NO WAY TO FLIP THE ROVER OVER, that's right, ones it's flipped it's stuck like that forever.

Needless to say, I've had the worst experience trying to get into this game and gotten nowhere because I've had to start again or load a save that many times - I given up.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the learning curve as steep, requiring external tutorials to understand core mechanics like conveyors, power systems, and basic ship building.

citations.review_text:
Space engineers is probably one of my favourite games of all time. I mostly enjoy meking massive ships in creative and then watching them crash. The crash phisics are pretty good with how blocks can be flattened and dented. Though the game doesn't have any orbital mechanics like KSP.

I do wish that there werent so many dlcs and it can get annoting to have to scroll through hundreds of things you dont own to find the ones you do in the building menu. Atleast the dlcs are cheap though.

The learning curve is also unfortunately more of a learning cliff and if your having trouble I recommend Splitsie's tutorials.

I bounced off this hard the first time because nothing explains itself, then came back a year later, watched a few Splitsie videos, and suddenly the conveyors and power grids clicked. Now I've got about 600 hours of watching my own ships tip over, grind into cliffsides, or explode the second I hit the launch button, and every failure taught me something the game never bothered to say out loud. The physics doing all the heavy lifting is what makes it special, since everything has mass and momentum and it will happily let you learn that the expensive way. My one real gripe is the DLC situation, because finding a cool derelict ship only to realize you can never repair half its blocks feels genuinely bad, and having them greyed out in the build menu instead of hidden is a weird choice. Still the best engineering sandbox on Steam, and I'll keep building in it anyway.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the initial gameplay involves a resource grind before players can advance to building ships.

citations.review_text: Very fun game, the initial grind is a bit boring but once you've got that down the games really fun,

It's a very slow game, especially if you're solo or even with just a duo. You'll more than likely want to play with a few friends or get used to making drills and such for much more resources quickly if you intend to get to the 'making cool ships' part of the game in survival.
I'm quite off and on with the game, but I do enjoy it overall and it is a very good game. Modding is  integrated into it so you can find really anything you could think of beyond just the base game. 
There are a lot of DLCs, however they're all exclusively cosmetic. Every major update comes with its own dlc pack, however any new features will always be free.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that multiplayer sessions frequently suffer from crashes, lag, and game-breaking bugs.

citations.review_text:
7 years since release, they still haven't figured out how to remember servers' passwords, prevent the game from randomly crashing, or let disable the startup intro. The game still lacks the most basic QOL functions like viewing the control panel name of the block you're looking at: you have to guess or use mods to do that. The interior wall mode has 15 THOUSAND polygons (when it only really needs 40 and some textures to look and feel the same), Just one room built from interior walls has more polygons than most in-game scenes in other games. Multiplayer has zero lag compensation. Every feature in the game has some sort of issue.

And yet, they are still pumping out worthless DLCs instead of fixing anything that's been broken for over half a decade.

There is a good game buried somewhere deep inside, but it's way overshadowed by developer's greed. The game gives you some basic tools to start building, but upon very first opening of the build menu you see that 90% of it is permanently grayed out, because it's all DLC content. Okay, I check in the store and turns out the total cost of DLCs as of the time of writing this reviews is 4x (FOUR TIMES) the price of the base game. This is some Paradoxical levels of greed

The game has been in development for a decade at this point, but still a buggy mess. I played multiplayer with friends and we didn't have a single session without someone encountering a game breaking issue of some sort. It seems that most of this development time was spent making DLCs

Overall, I can't recommend this game. To make an analogy, playing multiplayer will feel like you are having only cobblestone and oak planks, while the rest of the server got modern minecraft block assortment. Oh, and someone will crash every session, losing their inventory in a process

Very deep sandbox mechanics and tons of building options. The survival experience is pretty good as well. Multiplayer is unplayable if there is any lag at all. Unless you live very close to your friends, it will probably be a very poor experience. Expect a sandbox first, game second.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game has a steep learning curve and provides minimal guidance or hand-holding for new players.

citations.review_text:
Yeah... I say I recommend if you love building your dream ship.
Game is extremely well made. Devs are still updating the game even when sequal is currently in development.
And there are so many things you can build if you put your mind into it.

Only thing to note, with more complex builds. The doesn't hold your hand

10/10 - The most boring game I can't stop playing. 

Seriously though, this is a sandbox of make your own fun. Looking for a hand holding guided experience? This isn't it. Start with dirt, build an empire however you want. Manually, automated, whatever suits your play style. With friends, alone. 

Join themed servers, PVP other people. Lob rockets at them to say hello. Cut their fuel lines, plant warheads, rename all their blocks. Whatever you want, the universe is yours.
Steep learning curve, but so much to do and enjoy!
Great game. Huge learning curve but put in the time and it is worth it.

I have several problems with this game. 

Beyond a rather steep learning curve, this game has felt wholly incomplete for years, and has not gotten better as it has continued in its development. Additionally, I abhore games that add "updates" that provide functional necessity to the game in the form of purchasable DLC. As of posting this, that's currently an additonal $90+USD to obtain critical pieces, components, and features beyond the base game.

Gameplay is not intuitive, the vanilla "progression" makes little sense, and is needlessly frustrating. This game is so mind-bogglingly incomplete, the community seems to be constantly creating new mods to find, fix, and patch issues in the base game. I would be fine with the game if the problems were a skill issue or something that could be remedied with a tutorial, practice, or patience. Instead, the problems feel like the game punishing players for playing the game as it was intended.

My take of this game is what would happen if factorio/satisfactory met no mans sky, with a budget of $100 bucks to make it happen. Do not recommend.
This is a fantastic space sandbox or  space RPG - depending on your mood!  Slightly steep-ish learning curve, but a masterpiece once you get it.   10/10!
Very fun though it has a learning curve

If you are a dude with room temperature IQ, no testosterone because you beat you're dick everyday to furry porn and you wanna play a brain dead game like those gay ass clicking simulators on Roblox then this game isn't for you. For the ones that made it this far, congrats! This game can be overwhelming, there is a ton of moving parts. However you don't need to be a rocket scientist or even just be a science geek in general, I am a business major and I still figured it out. This game does demand one thing, COMMON SENSE and some critical thinking skills, (hence why I wanted to shoo away the bums still living in their moms basement). So if you're a man of culture who wants a survival challenge cause Minecraft is for cucks anyways then welcome to Space Engineers, and good luck! Your first hour is going to make you feel like someone shoved a whole science text book down you're throat and now YOU have to figure it out on you're own.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that performance suffers and the game can lag or tank when handling too many objects, players, or large complex builds.

citations.review_text: 10/10 game, just wish it could handle more objects/players without tanking. still love it though.

Not really a hard No or anything but this game would need to be pretty cheap to get the feeling you actually got enough to matter. Considering the Many, many DLCs and the core issues with the game I would just avoid this unless you have a specific desire for it. The game's build mechanic is Minecraftish meaning it is a cube regardless of shape and objects cannot intersect. Therefore you have EXTREEM limitations on building and forget making something you *want* because the other main issue is the complete failure to make engines *WORK* by the time you have enough to fly the thing is covered, looks stupid and needs to be trashed. Then there is the issue with the fact that the game is EMPTY, no "encounters" (unless constant dogs wandering into your base past defenses [no matter the settings] counts) even the spawned "locations" are just dead, VERY rarely there will be some minor thing to do like take this item to another dead location but that is it. Now you can buy some of the DLCs to liven this up a bit but not really...  So you decide to BUILD something... well no that too will be EXTREMLY limited the "PCU" count is collective and LOW at max settings, anything you build or the game wants to add to the emptiness counts together, the more you do the less the game does. You can store creations in a buildable terminal and that is nice but kind of meaningless unless you are playing with either creative mode or with Admin cheats, WHICH is the biggest saving grace the game has. claims.claim: Reviewers mention that buying all the DLC packs costs significantly more than the base game.

citations.review_text:
A different take on the DLCs

A lot of reviews criticize the DLCs, so here’s another view.

Yes, all the packs together add up to a lot of money, and I wouldn’t tell anyone just starting out to buy them. You don’t need them. They’re mostly cosmetic.

Many of us have been playing for 10+ years, and we don’t mind throwing Keen an extra five bucks once in a while. I paid less than $20 for the base game and have gotten over 1,000 hours out of it. That’s a great deal. And even while they’re working on Space Engineers 2, they’re still adding to the original.

Keen has been at this for about 13 years, and it has never felt like “aggressive monetization” to me, as one reviewer called it. If you’re looking at the game for the first time, I can see why it might look that way. But another pack comes out tomorrow, and I’ll happily give them my five bucks.

If you’re thinking about buying: I think the game is still worth it. The base game gives you so much to do that you don’t need to worry about the packs. Later on, look at the ones you’d actually enjoy and pick them up on sale. They seem to go on sale fairly often, and I didn’t pay full price for most of mine. I played for years before I bought my first one and never felt like I was missing out.

Hope that gives you another perspective on the DLCs and on a company that has been nothing but reasonable regarding prices.

Note, that i will talk about prices here. This applies to regional pricing in many countries. This game is pretty cool for what it is and has plenty of interesting mechanics and content. It requires a lot of creativity and is very rewarding. However it is not nearly worth the amount of money developers ask for it. They have some very aggressive monetization tactics. Each and every update they add a new DLC which adds a couple of new textures/models for blocks which costs a lot more than it should. Imagine you bought a creative game like minecraft. You expect full creative freedom, a lot of building blocks and features and intead you get a pack of basic cobblestone and wood blocks, stairs and slabs and all other building blocks are locked behind paid DLCs which in their entirety cost ~4 times more than the base game. Yes, you can build a house with those and you still can play the game with all its technical features, but you don't have nearly enough creative freedom. Yes, developers swear that all "gameplay" features/mechanics are always available for free in the base game, it's true, but when your core gameplay is BUILDING STUFF, and you can't build nearly as much pretty stuff without all the skins and blocks DLCs provide - you get frustrated. Base game has only around 25-30% of visual blocks available without DLCs. I do not recommend buying this game. It's NOT worth the full price you'll have to pay for it and it's DLCs

Even then, DLC blocks still show up in the menu without the DLC, and the only way to remove them is by adding another mod.
